name: Nguyen Trai
role: Staff scholar in the Lam Sơn uprising, drafter of proclamations, author of Bình Ngô sách and Bình Ngô đại cáo
known_facts: Held a modest post in the Lam Sơn staff, drafting proclamations as a hàn lâm học sĩ and serving as Hành khiển; not a front-line general
Author of Bình Ngô sách, whose core idea is 'tâm công' - attacking the enemy's mind and winning the people's hearts
During the siege of Đông Quan wrote streams of surrender letters to Vương Thông and to the commanders of the outlying garrisons; the Điêu Diêu and Nghệ An forts opened their gates without a fight
Alone opposed massacring the surrendered Ming army, arguing that revenge would only bring a fresh invasion and a longer war; Lê Lợi accepted and ordered the siege lifted
Ranked only 80th among the 93 công thần honoured after victory, far behind Phạm Vấn, Nguyễn Chích, Đinh Liệt and Lê Văn Linh
Author of Bình Ngô đại cáo, which recorded the campaign and its judgements
His opposition to revenge set him against generals who had buried comrades; the Lệ Chi Viên case came later
His true stature was recognised only by later generations
Native of Nhị Khê (Thường Tín, Hà Tây xưa); taught there before entering public life
1442: after Lê Thái Tông died suddenly at Lệ Chi Viên, Nguyễn Trãi was accused and executed with tru di tam tộc
1464: exonerated by Lê Thánh Tông, who had his writings gathered
Folk legend (giai thoại, not verified history): students clearing a mound disturbed a snake's nest; a white snake later dripped blood onto his book — told as a curse lasting three generations
interpretation: Early Later-Lê Vietnamese scholar-official dress based on the user reference.
unknowns: No verified contemporary life portrait survives
